name: Fernando Po Creole English

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Pichi (fern1234).
English lexifier, inherited via Krio: Pichi is a direct offshoot of the English-lexicon Krio of Sierra Leone, brought to Bioko by Krio settlers from Freetown in 1827 (Yakpo 2019; APiCS ch. 19).

Spanish adstrate, the co-official and sole educational-medium language of Equatorial Guinea: ~50% of nouns, ~30% of verbs and ~62% of numerals in the Pichi corpus are of Spanish origin, and code-mixing with Spanish is pervasive (Yakpo 2019; APiCS ch. 19, apics-online.info/surveys/19).

notes:
Research tier, consulting Yakpo's grammar of Pichi. English-lexifier Atlantic creole of Bioko (Equatorial Guinea), an offshoot of Krio, written in a Latin phonemic orthography. Grapheme map covers the seven-vowel system (a e ɛ i o ɔ u), the labial-velar stops kp/gb, and the digraphs ch, sh, ny and ng. Pichi contrasts two level tones, a high tone (H) and a low tone (L) (Yakpo 2019: 40, §3.1.1). No commonly accepted standard orthography is in use for Pichi (Yakpo 2019: 11, §1.6); marking tone on every word is the convention Yakpo adopts throughout his grammar, not a property of a settled working orthography. The seven H-toned vowel graphemes (á, é, í, ó, ú, ɛ́, ɔ́ — the last two written as base vowel plus combining acute, U+0301, since Latin has no precomposed ɛ́/ɔ́) are declared because the material transcribed in that convention carries them, and each maps to the identical H-toned IPA vowel. The plain vowel letters carry L tone, which the orthography leaves unmarked, and they map to grave-marked IPA vowels: L is unmarked in writing but not absent from the phonology, and a bare vowel would under-specify it. This is confirmed in the wikipron fpe gold, where all 261 words are fully toned — 249 carry at least one acute, 114 at least one grave, none carry neither, and of 1087 phone tokens the 391 vowel tokens split 259 H to 132 L with no untoned vowel at all.

Known gap: Yakpo (2019: 12, §1.6) ends the orthography section with 'Acute accents over Spanish words are orthographic, and hence not tone marks.' Spanish is the adstrate and supplies roughly half of Pichi nouns, so a Spanish-origin loan spelled with a stress acute should not receive H tone. This spec maps á é í ó ú to H unconditionally, because it has no lexicon with which to identify Spanish-origin words, so such loans are over-marked. The exception does not surface in the wikipron fpe gold: across all 261 words the acute count of the input string equals the H-tone count of the gold transcription in every row, giving zero counterexamples to measure against.
